**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: P1 slice of RWB-DM-005 for rwb-source-data — the one-off cutover load of the Workbench contact notes and open promises held outside EFS into this service's own `interaction` and `contact_point_ext`, the no-copy boundary of the EFS history, the ten clean days and the sign-off; legacy AC1 and AC2 move to RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG and this story owns legacy AC3. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **data steward (RW-DATASTEW)** and a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the open promises and contact notes the legacy Workbench holds outside EFS extracted once at cutover and loaded into this service's own `interaction` and `contact_point_ext` tables in `rwb_source_data`, each interaction keeping its case, its person key, its contact key, its promise date and its promise amount, with the EFS history read from `v_ace_efs_action` and never copied, and the ten clean days and the sign-off recorded as the cutover evidence**, so that **no promise a customer made is lost at cutover while the EFS history itself is read from ACE**.

**This is the P1 slice of legacy RWB-DM-005, not a withdrawal of it.** The legacy key keeps its epic E1, its release 30 November 2026 and its decision DL25; the realignment changes who owns the rows. The interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18; ASM-0067), `contact_point_ext` is one of the four extension tables P1 owns (Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P1 v3 T3.5), and DP05 Contact and promises names `interaction` with the three EFS views as its reads (FSD P1 v3 A2.2). `recovery_case` is P3 rwb-case's and is read through its contract, never written (DP-01). The slice is exactly four things: the one-off cutover load of the two tables on this service's login and per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), the no-copy boundary of the EFS history, the ten clean days counted from the `reconciliation_result` rows of JOB-04, and the sign-off that closes the cutover.

**What this story does not build.** No REST operation of its own, no Kafka event, no workflow, no Schedule and no screen: the cutover is one-off bulk work from the release pipeline, and its result and breaks are read on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and SCR-45 Data quality through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 32). Section 12 says so table by table.

##### 2. Business rationale

A promise date or amount lost at cutover cannot be recovered afterwards: the customer keeps a commitment the bank no longer sees, the arrears strategy runs on a wrong date, and the next call opens with no record of what was agreed. The opposite risk is as costly: a copy of the EFS history into the Workbench makes the two stores drift, holds personal data under a retention rule the Workbench does not own, and answers the same case twice. The legacy story says what it protects:

> **Epic** E1, release 30 November 2026 · **Module** P1 Recovery data engine · **Depends on** RWB-E1-001, RWB-E1-069 · **Decision** DL25
>
> **Story** As a data steward, I want the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS migrated to the case, so that no promise a customer made is lost at cutover while the EFS history itself is read from ACE.

**Why this service loads its own tables.** Three ownership facts agree here: Architecture v5 slide 41 and the default ruling put the interaction ledger with rwb-source-data (DP-18; ASM-0067); the FSD gives DP05 `interaction` with the three EFS views (refresh DAILY, expected by 08:00); and the TSD defines `contact_point_ext` as a P1 extension table keyed by `contact_key`, holding a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of it (TSD P1 v3 T3.5). The service that owns the rows reads the dump and writes on its own login, with no handover and no C dependency of its own.

**Why the EFS history is read and never copied.** EFS is ingested into ACE (INT-07, owner the ACE team: TSD P1 v3 T5.1) and read through views 9, 10 and 11; the monolith copy `collections_history` is removed as a copy of EFS data (TSD P1 v3 T3.10; D-RCV-35 U1), and DL29 keeps twelve months readable. The Workbench holds the promise the customer made to us; ACE holds the contact history that was always ACE's. The extract therefore refuses a legacy row whose EFS record key resolves to a view row (legacy AC1, owned by RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG).

**Why ten clean days, and why the load is idempotent.** The cutover ends when the moved rows are seen to reconcile day after day: JOB-04 writes one `reconciliation_result` row per check and product group, REC-05 included (FSD P1 v3 A2.11; TSD P1 v3 T3.6). Ten consecutive clean days, with a break resetting the count, is that evidence; the count, the record that holds it and the sign-off shape are not fixed beyond AC3, so they are one assumption rather than an invention (GAP-2166; ASM-3477). And because the ledger is append only with no update path (RWB-P1-E1066-APP), each legacy row carries its own record key and the load is idempotent on it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- **The views exist and are granted.** RWB-P1-E1069-APP creates the Section A views on the per-service sequence, views 9 to 11 with fields `DF-ACE-108` to `DF-ACE-139` among them (TSD P1 v3 T3.2, T3.3), and the `rwb_source_data` login holds SELECT on them and nothing in `public` (TSD P1 v3 T6.3).
- **The two target tables exist.** `interaction` arrives with RWB-P1-E1001-APP and its ledger shape, unique keys, sequence allocator and append-only trigger with RWB-P1-E1066-APP; `contact_point_ext` arrives with RWB-P1-E1069-DB (TSD P1 v3 T3.5). This story creates and alters neither.
- **The reconciliation writes its rows.** JOB-04, its REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 checks and `reconciliation_result` belong to RWB-P1-E1011-APP; until it lands a fixture stands in for the rows the count reads (12.8).
- **The per-service Flyway contract is in place.** RWB-PLT-E1044-CON gives the sequence with its `V0001` baseline and the view versions (DP-15); this story takes the next free version and creates nothing in it.
- **The gateway-bff composite route exists**, because RWB-PLT-N001-CON is the H dependency of DP-19: the result and its breaks are read through a route, not stitched by a screen.
- **The cutover has a place to run.** The release pipeline runs it for one business date against the service's own API and never touches a `rwb_*` schema (Architecture v5 slide 32). **The pipeline step name, the cutover record format and the dump layout:** Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2166; ASM-3474).
- **No dependency blocks the start.** The two platform stories are contract stories and the two P1 stories are in-lane APP work, so the story starts after RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-APP (§R5.7 rules 2, 3 and 8); the wave 4 tag is the W-MAP tag of EP08 and does not delay the build.

##### 4. Flow

1. The cutover window opens; the release pipeline starts the step for one business date and one environment as one-off bulk work through this service's own admin operation. No scheduler runs it.
2. CutoverContactPromiseExtract reads the legacy cutover dump once, only for the promises and notes held outside EFS: the case rows of their cases (`DF-CAS-001` to `DF-CAS-055`), their `interaction` rows (`DF-INT-001` to `DF-INT-029`) and the `contact_point_ext` rows of their contact keys (`DF-EXT-013` to `DF-EXT-026`).
3. EfsDuplicateGuard reads `v_ace_efs_action` (view 9) once for the account keys of the extract and refuses every legacy row whose EFS record key resolves to a view row; action codes are carried as held and checked against `v_ace_efs_action_code` (view 10), with none minted and none translated.
4. InteractionCutoverMapper maps each remaining interaction to its case and keeps the five facts whole — case, `person_key`, `contact_key`, `promise_date`, `promise_amount` — copying and deriving nothing and inventing no `party_id` or `contact_point_id` (ASM-3475).
5. CaseContractCheck calls the P3 case read for each case and refuses the batch when a case does not answer, so no migrated row points at a case the case service does not serve; the answer is a mock in the tests and adds no C dependency (12.2).
6. ContactPromiseCutoverLoader inserts both tables in one transaction per cutover business date: one `interaction` row per note or promise through the ledger's sequence allocator, with `source_system` and `source_ref` carrying what the legacy row holds; one `contact_point_ext` row per contact key, with consent carried as `consent_given` plus `consent_at` — WITHDRAWN as false with its date, UNKNOWN as no row at all (TSD P1 v3 T3.5).
7. CutoverEvidenceReader reads the `reconciliation_result` rows JOB-04 writes after the load (`DF-OPS-118` to `DF-OPS-129`) and counts the clean days: a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan adds a day; a BREAK row or new orphan resets the count to zero and names the day.
8. On the tenth consecutive clean day the data steward signs off, held in the cutover record beside the ten day rows; the legacy tables are then set read-only for their retention period and the records are served from the new schema through this service's interaction read.
9. At deploy the version applies on the per-service sequence, writes one `flyway_schema_history` row and creates no table, column or index; its description carries the extract definition, the field list, the legacy record key and the read-only window (DP-15).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The dump is absent, unreadable or read twice for the same business date | The step stops before any mapping; no row is written and the record names the date and the reason | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X2 | An interaction carries no case, or its case does not answer | The row is refused whole, the step stops and the record names the row and the case; no partial load | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X3 | A required key is empty: case, `person_key`, `contact_key`, `promise_date`, `promise_amount`, `contact_type` or `source_system` | The row is refused whole with the field named; no default and no derived value | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X4 | `v_ace_efs_action` holds the EFS record key a legacy row carries | The legacy row is not migrated — that history is read from the view — and is counted as skipped | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A view read fails: relation absent or statement error | The step stops with no partial load and no stale history carried as current | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The transaction of a business date fails during the load | Nothing of that date is committed; the rerun is idempotent on the legacy record key | None | AC3 |
| X7 | JOB-04 writes a BREAK row or a new orphan for a migrated record during the ten days | The count resets to zero, the day is named and the break is listed; the sign-off cannot be recorded | None | AC3 |

The message texts are the legacy ones (section 14). MSG-P1-001 is raised by the freshness read of this service when the EFS batch is late; this story asserts it and does not produce it.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | One extract reader, one duplicate guard, one mapper, one case check, one loader, one evidence reader and one migration; the case is mocked |
| Negotiable | The dump layout and the cutover record are agreed at the rehearsal; this story fixes only the five facts, the no-copy rule and the idempotency key |
| Valuable | Every promise and consent held outside EFS survives cutover in the schema that now owns it, evidenced by ten clean days |
| Estimable | One batch step, five components, one migration, five fixtures and two test cases |
| Small | Fits one sprint, as the P1 slice of a split legacy key |
| Testable | AC3 runs end to end on a synthetic extract and synthetic reconciliation rows; no production and no ACE data needed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Migrate contact and promises

  Scenario: AC3 Cut over (legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3)
    Given ten clean days on the migrated records
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case of each migrated interaction
    When the data steward signs off
    Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period
    And the migrated records are served from the new schema
```

AC3 is copied character for character from legacy RWB-DM-005. The added Given is the rwb-case contract answer — the case of each interaction is read through the contract and never from a table — and it changes no legacy value in the When or Then lines. AC1 Extract the Workbench records and AC2 Reconcile the business keys are owned by RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG and are claimed by neither this file nor this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The interaction ledger is P1's in `rwb_source_data` and is written only by this service; `recovery_case` is P3's, read through its contract and never written | ASM-0067; DP-01, DP-18; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | `contact_point_ext` is P1's extension table keyed by `contact_key`, holding a Workbench decision about an ACE record; this story writes its rows and copies no ACE column into it | TSD P1 v3 T3.5; FSD P1 v3 A2.2; DP-01 |
| BR3 | The EFS history is read from `v_ace_efs_action`, `v_ace_efs_action_code` and `v_ace_efs_assignment` and never copied; a legacy row whose EFS record key resolves to a view row is not migrated | Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1; DL29; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.10; REQ-RDF-003 |
| BR4 | A migrated interaction keeps its case, `person_key`, `contact_key`, promise date and promise amount; no value is derived or defaulted | Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 (owned by RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG); TSD P3 v3 T3.1 |
| BR5 | The load is idempotent on the legacy record key: a second run of the same business date inserts no row and reports it as already loaded | AC3; RWB-P1-E1066-APP (append-only ledger) |
| BR6 | Ten clean days are counted from the `reconciliation_result` rows of JOB-04 on the migrated records; a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new orphan adds a day and a break resets the count | Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11; DL25; ASM-3477 |
| BR7 | The sign-off is held in the cutover record, the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period, and the records are served from the new schema | Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3; REQ-RDF-013; ASM-3474 |
| BR8 | The service runs its own Flyway sequence in its own schema; this story's version creates no table, no column and no index | DP-15; ADR-021; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 |
| BR9 | ACE data is read only through `recovery.v_ace_*` views, on the service's own login, SELECT only, with no `public` table in any statement | BR-P1-001-2, BR-P1-001-4; ADR-010; DP-05; TSD P1 v3 T6.3 |
| BR10 | A business key with no view row is an orphan: listed for the data steward and, where the row is missing in ACE, for the ACE team, and it never deletes or changes the record | BR-P1-011-3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.3.1; REQ-RDF-008 |
| BR11 | No value a business person may change is written in code, and no personal data appears in the extract, a log, a fixture or a prompt | Legacy RWB-DM-005 guardrails; FSD P1 v3 BR-P1-011; §R7.2 s17 |

BR1 and BR2 are the schema of `rwb_source_data`, proved by the load's own inserts and by the absence of any write to `rwb_case`; BR3 by the guard and by no ledger row mirroring an EFS action; BR4 on the load row; BR5 by the unique key on the source reference; BR6 and BR7 by the cutover evidence; BR8 by the migration; BR9 by the grant and boundary test of RWB-P1-E1069-DB; BR10 by the reconciliation the count relies on; BR11 by the review rule for the cutover code and its fixtures.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case: this story changes no case status, stage, task or promise state. The moves are the cutover's own, and they are six.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cutover not started | The step is started for the business date | The dump is readable and every case of the extract is in it | Extract ready |
| Extract ready | The loader commits the business date | Every row carries its five facts and its legacy record key | Loaded: rows in both tables |
| Loaded | The loader is started again for the same business date | The legacy record key is already present | Loaded, unchanged: nothing inserted, the repeat reported |
| Loaded | JOB-04 writes PASS rows for the migrated records | No unexplained variance and no new orphan on the day | Ten clean days running, at the consecutive count |
| Ten clean days running | A BREAK row or a new orphan appears | The break is listed for the data steward | Ten clean days running, at zero |
| Ten clean days running | The tenth clean day is reached and the steward signs off | The sign-off is recorded in the cutover record | Signed off: tables read-only, records served from the new schema |

The cutover record is the ledger of each move and the Flyway history row is the schema's record of the deploy; this story publishes no event for any move.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Runs the cutover for a business date, owns the ten day evidence and records the sign-off (FSD P1 v3 A2.11.3.3) |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Hold the Platform administration right R of the legacy permission check and may read the record, the evidence and the extract for their scope (TSD P1 v3 T6.1) |
| RW-TRIBE, squad member | Builds the components and applies the version on the per-service sequence |
| The rwb-source-data service identity (`rwb_source_data` login) | Reads views 9 to 11 and the reconciliation rows, writes the migrated rows and its own history row |
| P3 rwb-case and its identity | Owns `recovery_case` and answers the case read; this story takes no right over the table |

The role codes are rows of rwb-access and the step authorises through the guard of the published admin operation; this story adds no role and no grant.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055 | `recovery_case` | The case of each interaction and its business keys | Read from the legacy dump and the P3 case contract; P3 owns the table and this story writes no row of it |
| DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029 | `interaction` | All 29 fields, `case_id`, `occurred_at`, `action_code`, `promise_date`, `promise_amount`, `source_system`, `source_ref` first | Write, one row per note or promise, at the cutover only; no update, no delete |
| DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026 | `contact_point_ext` | `contact_key`, `contact_type`, `consent_given`, `consent_at`, `verified_at`, `failed_count`, `source` and the standard columns | Write, one row per contact key of a migrated interaction, at the cutover only |
| DF-ACE-108 to DF-ACE-127 | `v_ace_efs_action` | 20 fields of view 9, `efs_record_key` and `account_key` first | Read only, for the duplicate guard; never written, never copied |
| DF-ACE-128 to DF-ACE-130 | `v_ace_efs_action_code` | The 3 fields of view 10 | Read only, to check a carried action code against LOV-ACTION-CODE |
| DF-ACE-131 to DF-ACE-139 | `v_ace_efs_assignment` | The 9 fields of view 11, keyed by `account_key` | Read only, for the hand-over history of a promise account |
| DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129 | `reconciliation_result` | The 12 fields of a reconciliation row | Read for the count; written by JOB-04, never here |

Field IDs are those of TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.5 and T3.6 and of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The migrated row is a legacy Workbench fact and never a copy of an ACE row: the ACE side of a promise stays in `v_ace_efs_action` (BR3). One point is not settled — the legacy data row names `person_key` and `contact_key` while the ledger defines `party_id` and `contact_point_id` as cross-references and carries no column of either name, so **where the two business keys are held is** Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2166; ASM-3475). The seven standard record columns of TSD P1 v3 T3.0 are carried by both target tables and never by a view.

##### 12. Contract

**12.1 REST operations provided**

None. The cutover is one-off bulk work from the release pipeline and is not a public operation: this story adds no path, no query parameter and no response field. The admin and reconciliation operations it is started and read by, and the interaction read its tests use, belong to other RWB-SVC-P1 stories and are named in 12.2, not claimed here (Architecture v5 slide 32).

**12.2 REST operations consumed**

None at run time by this story's own code. The step is started and its result read by the pipeline through this service's own operations, and the case is a mock in the tests:

| Caller | Operation | Owner | Why it is not a dependency of this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| The release pipeline | `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` for the cutover job of a business date | P1 rwb-source-data | Same service: an in-lane operation, held by the story that publishes it |
| The release pipeline | `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions` for the reconciliation extract | P1 rwb-source-data | Same service; the cutover record reads its evidence from it |
| The tests | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Contract mock only; the extract carries the case as the dump holds it |
| The tests | `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1068-APP) | Same service: proves the records are served from the new schema |

The story therefore holds no C dependency and no I dependency. DP-11 is not one of its patterns: there is no outbound call to build against, so no timeout of its own is added beyond the platform's one hop and 2 s.

**12.3 Events published**

None. The cutover writes no outbox row and adds no schema to `rwb.source-data.events.v1`; `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to this service's freshness stories (TSD P1 v3 T5.3).

**12.4 Events consumed**

None. The step is started for a business date by the release pipeline; it reads no topic and no inbox row, and the `reconciliation_result` rows it counts are read from the table.

**12.5 Workflows and activities**

None added. JOB-04 Reconciliation is an event-triggered workflow of this service, exercised through its rows and unchanged. The cutover is a batch job of the release pipeline, not a Temporal workflow, because it runs once per cutover business date and not on a schedule or an event.

**12.6 Schedules**

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits here; JOB-04 is started by `AceDataReady` and belongs to RWB-P1-E1011-APP.

**12.7 Tables owned**

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interaction` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 (ASM-0067; DP-18) | Write at the cutover: one INSERT per note or promise, idempotent on the legacy record key, through the ledger's sequence allocator; no UPDATE, no DELETE |
| `contact_point_ext` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Write at the cutover: one row per contact key of a migrated interaction, with the standard columns |
| `flyway_schema_history` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | One row for its own version at deploy |
| `recovery_case` | `rwb_case` | P3 | Not written: read through the P3 contract only (DP-01) |
| `reconciliation_result` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Not written here: read for the count, written by JOB-04 |

Two tables are written and three are not, and that split is the boundary. That `contact_point_ext` is written here at all is the one point the sources do not settle: the FSD files it under DP02 and gives DP05 only `interaction`, while the legacy data row of this key carries the consent and quality rows, so the load stays with the slice that holds them (GAP-2166; ASM-3476). No statement names a `public` table, another service's schema or a cross-schema foreign key (DP-01, DP-05), and the append-only rule is respected, so a wrong row is corrected by its own record and not by an edit.

**12.8 Contract fakes**

| Fake | Serves | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy cutover extract fixture | The notes and promises held outside EFS, as synthetic rows with their cases, person keys, contact keys and promises | AC3, from Day 1, with no legacy data |
| View fixture (`v_ace_efs_action`, `v_ace_efs_action_code`, `v_ace_efs_assignment`) | Synthetic EFS rows: one series matching a legacy EFS record key and one matching none, with the action code list | AC3 and the skip path of X4 |
| rwb-case contract mock | The case of each migrated interaction, and one case that does not answer | AC3 and the refusal path of X2 |
| Reconciliation extract fixture | The `reconciliation_result` rows: PASS, BREAK and the REC-05 orphan | AC3 and the reset path of X7 |
| P1 interaction read mock | The migrated records served from `rwb_source_data` | AC3, in the last Then line |

Each fake is generated from the published contract it fronts or from the fixture set agreed at the rehearsal, so a contract change shows up as a test failure. The fixture layouts and the dump file name are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2166; ASM-3474).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.cutover`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema and login `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data`; the topic and the queue are named for completeness and this story uses neither.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CutoverContactPromiseExtract | Batch job | The one-off read of the dump for the promises and notes held outside EFS; one pass per business date |
| EfsDuplicateGuard | Service | One SELECT on `v_ace_efs_action` and the refusal of every row whose EFS record key resolves to a view row; no copy, no write |
| InteractionCutoverMapper | Service | Maps each interaction to its case and keeps the five facts whole, carrying the two business keys |
| CaseContractCheck | Client | One call of the P3 case read per case, 2 s and a breaker, so no row points at a case the service does not serve |
| ContactPromiseCutoverLoader | Repository | The only write path: inserts both tables for one business date in one transaction, idempotent on the legacy record key |
| CutoverEvidenceReader | Service | Counts the clean days, resets on a break, and holds the ten day rows beside the sign-off |
| The next free version of the per-service sequence | Migration | Creates no object; records the extract definition, field list, legacy record key and read-only window in its description |

**Pattern application**

| DP code | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies in its own-service form: this is the service that owns the views, so the EFS reads are its own SQL on its own login and add no contract hop (Architecture v5 slide 45; ADR-010). DP-15 gives the sequence the version runs on and the history row that records the cutover definition, and is also why the load is this service's and not a handover. DP-19 puts the result and its breaks behind the composite routes of SCR-44 and SCR-45. No other pattern applies: no event (DP-09), no parameter or reference read (DP-06, DP-07), no guard library of its own (DP-08), no outbound call (DP-11), no cross-service adapter (DP-16) and no rule evaluation (DP-04).

**Database and migrations.** The story reads views 9 to 11 and the `reconciliation_result` rows and writes `interaction`, `contact_point_ext` and its own history row; no other table of any schema is named. The version creates no table, column, index or constraint — `interaction` comes from RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1066-APP and `contact_point_ext` from RWB-P1-E1069-DB (BR8). No grant is made or changed: the login and its SELECT on the 30 views are RWB-P1-E1069-DB's. The version number is the next free one on the sequence and is not fixed here (TSD P1 v3 T3.2; ADR-021).

**Configuration and reference data.** No parameter and no reference list is read: DP-06 and DP-07 are not patterns of this story, and the ten day target, the business date and the retention period are data of the cutover record, not constants. The feature switch is `rwb.source-data.dm005-cutover-extract` from the platform flag library: off, the step refuses to start and no row is written, while the migration still applies because it creates nothing (ASM-3478).

**Build steps**

1. Extract over the cutover fixture, one pass per business date, with the absent-dump and double-read cases; AC3 and X1.
2. Guard over the three view fixtures, one row whose EFS record key matches and one that matches nothing, proving the match is skipped and no view field is written; AC3 and X4.
3. Mapper and case check: five facts whole, two business keys kept, no derived value or default, and one case that does not answer; AC3, X2 and X3.
4. Loader: one transaction per business date, the sequence allocator, the consent mapping of GIVEN, WITHDRAWN and UNKNOWN, the repeat run that inserts nothing, and the rollback of X6; AC3 and X6.
5. Evidence reader: ten PASS rows count up, a BREAK row or a new orphan resets the count, and the sign-off is refused below ten; AC3 and X7.
6. The version on the next free sequence as a no-op on the schema, plus the repeated-apply check, and the refusal path through the guard of the admin operation; AC3 and TC-DM-005-04.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the migrated promises and consents answer from `rwb_source_data` through this service's own read and no EFS row has been copied, AC3 counts ten clean days and records the sign-off, a repeat of the same business date inserts nothing, and no class of the service names a `public` table or another service's schema.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | When | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | The extract lacks a required field or record: a case, a person key, a contact key, a promise date, a promise amount or a contact type | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | A caller without the Platform administration right starts the cutover step | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | Warning | The EFS feed behind DP05 is late for the business date, so the history cannot be carried as current | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |

The three messages are copied character for character from the legacy master (legacy RWB-DM-005 validation table; FSD P1 v3 VR-P1-011-1; TSD P1 v3 T3.7). This story raises MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P4-002 itself: {field} is the field or record the extract lacks, and {action} is "run the contact and promise cutover extract", never a case fact or a value. MSG-P1-001 is raised by the freshness read of this service and asserted here as evidence.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The cutover is started and its result read on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, and the breaks that reset the count are shown on SCR-45 Data quality, which RWB-P1-AD019-APP owns. Both are read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); this story adds no route, field or rendering, and the route path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2166; ASM-3474).

| State | What the cutover record holds | What the monitor shows |
|---|---|---|
| Extract ready | Business date, rows read, rows refused as EFS duplicates, cases resolved | The step is running and the extract is ready |
| Loaded | Rows written per table, with their legacy record keys | The rows are in `rwb_source_data` and answer through this service's read |
| Repeated run | Rows already present, rows written as zero, business date | The rerun completed and nothing was duplicated |
| Ten clean days running | Consecutive clean days and the last clean day | The count, its date and the remaining days |
| Break | The BREAK row or orphan, its date, code and owner role, count at zero | The break is listed and the count is reset |
| Signed off | The ten day rows, the extract, the sign-off and the read-only window | The cutover is complete and the legacy tables are read-only |

A cutover that has not reached ten clean days shows as a count and not as a pass, so one break in the window is visible as a reset and the sign-off cannot be recorded below ten (AC3).

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is recorded in the Recovery Workbench Test Cases workbook, tab Story test cases, under the same ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the five facts are data on the load row, and the ten day target, the business date and the retention period are data of the cutover record, never a constant, an amount or a date in a class.
- No personal data in the extract, the logs, the fixtures or the prompts: it carries case and promise facts and ACE business keys, and no customer name, phone number, e-mail address or identity field; the fixtures are synthetic (BR11).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, and here the service is the owner of the views: one login, SELECT only, no `public` table in any statement (BR9).
- No copy of an ACE row: the EFS history is read through views 9 to 11 and never copied, and a legacy row that resolves to an EFS record is not migrated at all (BR3).
- No cross-schema write and no cross-schema join: `recovery_case` is read through the P3 contract and no statement names `rwb_case` (BR1; DP-01).
- The ledger is append only and one version on the per-service sequence is never edited in place: the load inserts, never updates and never deletes, and a later change is a new version (BR5, BR8).
- A cutover is never declared on a count that has been reset: a break sets the count to zero and the sign-off stays closed (BR6, BR7).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-DM-005 for the wave 4 cutover reconciliation harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **data steward**, I want **a repeatable wave 4 cutover reconciliation harness that proves every business key on the migrated contact and promise records resolves to its ACE view row, that the EFS history is read and never copied, and that every orphan is listed for the data steward and the ACE team, against the owning services' published contracts and their fakes**, so that **no promise a customer made is lost at cutover while the EFS history itself is read from ACE**.

This story builds a test harness and its evidence only. Legacy AC1 and AC2 are proved here; legacy AC3, the cut-over sign-off, stays with RWB-P1-DM005-APP, which also owns the rwb-source-data code, the REC-05 step, the per-service Flyway sequence that carries the cutover load (DP-15) and every migration write. The harness seeds nothing by hand: on Day 1 the stub set of section 12.8 returns the migrated records, and in SIT the cutover load of rwb-source-data's own Flyway sequence provides them, so a passed run means the owner's contract and its data are right and not that the harness wrote a row.

##### 2. Business rationale

A promise date or a promise amount that disappears at cutover cannot be recovered afterwards: the customer keeps a commitment the bank no longer sees, the arrears strategy runs on a wrong date, and the officer opens the next call with no record of what was agreed. The second risk is the opposite one. If the EFS history is copied into the Workbench instead of read from the ACE views, the two stores drift and the bank holds a personal-data copy it cannot defend under a retention rule it does not own. The third is a contact point whose contact key has no ACE row: an orphan used anyway is a contact attempt on a record nobody can trace.

That is why the legacy criterion carries zero tolerance. DL25 sets zero tolerance for reconciliation breaks on the migrated data, and REQ-RDF-007 and REQ-RDF-008 require that every business key resolves to its ACE row and that every break is listed for the data product owner. The cutover is decoupled the way the target is: the harness reads the migrated records through rwb-source-data's contract and never a table (DP-05), the cutover load is the owner's own per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15), the evidence is the harness's own report and not a screen, every call is one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-11), and JOB-04 is triggered through the owner's rerun operation because it is an event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data and not a shared job table.

The EFS history stays where ACE put it. DL29 keeps twelve months of it, read through v_ace_efs_action, so the Workbench holds the promise the customer made to us and ACE holds the contact history that was always ACE's, and no copy of either drifts.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The rwb-source-data contract is published with the data product record reads of DP02 and DP05, the freshness read, the JOB-04 rerun operation and the interaction read, and a WireMock stub set is generated from it.
- The P3 rwb-case contract is published with the case read, and its stub set is generated from it.
- The data product catalog holds DP02 Customer and party and DP05 Contact and promises with ACE named as the system of record, and DP05 names v_ace_efs_action, v_ace_efs_action_code and v_ace_efs_assignment as the ACE reads (FSD P1 v3).
- RWB-P1-DM005-APP is the integration dependency and is not required on Day 1: until it lands the harness runs against the stub set, and the run report says so. In SIT the cutover load of rwb-source-data's own Flyway sequence (DP-15) has carried the migrated contact and promise records for the business date under test.
- The harness environment and its base hosts, the synthetic cutover extract fixture and its field layout, the reconciliation extract format and its retention, the pass or fail gate and the data seeding set are: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).
- The harness runs in SIT only, with a report per business date, and it opens no schema and no ACE view: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the fakes in place from the first run, and the stub replaced by the real owner as RWB-P1-DM005-APP lands.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: builds the run fixture and the stub set. On Day 1 the section 12.8 stubs return the migrated records; in SIT the cutover load of rwb-source-data's own Flyway sequence (DP-15) has already provided them, and the harness seeds nothing by hand.
2. Harness: triggers JOB-04 for business date 2026-11-30 through `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` on the owner's base, one hop with one Idempotency-Key, and never a Schedule or a job table of its own (DP-11).
3. Harness: reads interaction `INT-0605` and its promise facts through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` on case `RW-2026-000605`, and asserts the case, person_key `PERS-SYN-0605`, contact_key `CP-SYN-0605`, promise date 2026-12-15 and promise amount 12500 are the ones the cutover extract holds.
4. Harness: reads the case through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` on rwb-case and asserts the case number, stage and primary person key, so the migrated record points at a case the owner serves.
5. Harness: resolves the person key and the contact key through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP02/records?caseId={caseId}`, and reads the promise and the EFS history through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP05/records?caseId={caseId}` with `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP05`, one hop each with a 2 s budget.
6. Harness: asserts that no EFS contact or promise row is copied. The EFS history is read from v_ace_efs_action, the DP05 record names its source and its migration date, and the interaction ledger holds no row that mirrors an EFS action.
7. Harness: reads the break list from the reconciliation extract for business date 2026-11-30, which is where the legacy story says the breaks are listed, and asserts one row for interaction `INT-0605` with key type CONTACT, key value `CP-SYN-0777`, reason `NO_ACE_ROW` and owner role `RW-DATASTEW`, and that no contact was attempted on that contact point.
8. Harness: reruns JOB-04 for the same business date with a second Idempotency-Key, then compares the counts of interactions and of their promise links with the first run and asserts the break list holds exactly one row for `CP-SYN-0777`, and that the run report holds one entry per business date and not one per run.
9. Harness: calls the reconciliation run as the RW-OFF caller and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002, no run started and no break row written, then publishes the report of the business date with the four criteria, their assertions, the contract versions and whether each hop was a stub or the owner.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | The cutover extract fixture lacks a required key: case, person_key, contact_key, promise date or promise amount | The run fails before any assertion and the report names the field and the fixture row | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A key with no ACE view row is not listed on the reconciliation extract | The run fails on AC2 and AC3 and the report names the key and the business date | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X4 | A break row is listed twice after the rerun | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the break row and both run identifiers | None | AC4 |
| X5 | JOB-04 refuses to run because the DP05 freshness is late | The run is reported as not started, no break row is written, and the report names the product and its data date | MSG-P1-001 | AC1, AC2 |
| X6 | An EFS row appears in the interaction ledger as a copy | The run fails on AC1 regardless of the promise facts, and the report names the ledger row | None | AC1 |
| X7 | A caller without the Platform administration right starts a run anyway | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the caller role and the operation | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The messages in section 14 are asserted as the answers of the owning service, not produced by the harness.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against published contracts and fakes from Day 1; its only wait is RWB-P1-DM005-APP, and each criterion runs before and after it lands |
| Negotiable | The fixtures, the break-list read and the report shape are configuration and agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The proof that no promise is lost and no EFS history is copied at cutover, which no single service story can show |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one stub set, two fixtures, one key resolver, one break-list assertion and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its four test cases |
| Testable | Each criterion is one automated test against the fakes and again against the real owner |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Migrate contact and promises - wave 4 cutover reconciliation harness

  Background:
    Given the synthetic cutover extract holds open promise "INT-0605" on case "RW-2026-000605" with person_key "PERS-SYN-0605", contact_key "CP-SYN-0605", promise date "2026-12-15" and promise amount "12500"
    Given the ACE EFS view holds contact history for person_key "PERS-SYN-0605"
    Given JOB-04 has run for business date "2026-11-30"

  Scenario: AC1 Extract the Workbench records (legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1)
    Given the open promises and contact notes that the legacy Workbench holds outside EFS, with their case numbers
    When the migration reads them
    Then each interaction keeps its case, its person_key, its contact_key, its promise date and its promise amount
    And no EFS contact or promise row is copied, because the history is read from v_ace_efs_action

  Scenario: AC2 Reconcile the business keys (legacy RWB-DM-005 AC2)
    Given the migrated records
    When the REC-05 step runs
    Then every business key on a migrated record resolves to its view row, account_key and person_key included
    And each orphan is listed for the data steward and the ACE team

  Scenario: AC3 An orphan contact key is listed and no contact is attempted (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given migrated interaction "INT-0605" carries contact_key "CP-SYN-0777"
    And the ACE contact view holds no row for contact_key "CP-SYN-0777"
    When the harness reads the reconciliation result for business date "2026-11-30"
    Then the break list holds one row for interaction "INT-0605" with key type "CONTACT" and key value "CP-SYN-0777"
    And the row names the reason "NO_ACE_ROW" and the owner role "RW-DATASTEW"
    And no contact is attempted on the orphan contact point
    And the interaction stays readable through the rwb-source-data contract

  Scenario: AC4 A repeated run is deterministic and one break is listed once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the reconciliation for business date "2026-11-30" has run once
    When JOB-04 is rerun for the same business date
    Then the break list holds exactly one row for contact_key "CP-SYN-0777"
    And the counts of interactions and their promise links equal the first run
    And the run report holds one entry per business date and not one per run

  Scenario: AC5 A caller without the platform administration right is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic user with role "RW-OFF" and no Platform administration right
    When the harness calls the reconciliation run for business date "2026-11-30"
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no reconciliation run starts and no break row is written
```

Legacy AC3 belongs to RWB-P1-DM005-APP, and the five criteria above are the ones this ITG story owns.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every business key on a migrated contact or promise record resolves to its ACE view row, account_key and person_key included | REQ-RDF-007; DL25 |
| BR2 | Every break is listed for the data steward and the ACE team, with the key type, the key value, the reason and the owner role | REQ-RDF-008 |
| BR3 | Zero tolerance: one orphan on the migrated data is a break and is never waived | DL25 |
| BR4 | ACE data is read only through the views and the contract owned by rwb-source-data, and no service or harness reads an ACE view directly | D-RCV-35; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | The EFS history is read from v_ace_efs_action and never copied, so the Workbench holds the Workbench promise and ACE holds the EFS history | DL29; legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 |
| BR6 | A migrated record keeps its source and its migration date, and never a copy of an ACE row | legacy RWB-DM-005 guardrails |
| BR7 | The cutover load is the per-service Flyway sequence of the owning service and no other load path exists | DP-15 |

##### 9. State transitions

The harness changes no state. The interaction keeps its promise date 2026-12-15 and its promise amount 12500 before, during and after every run, and the case keeps its stage and its primary person key. An orphan contact point stays readable through the rwb-source-data contract and is listed on the reconciliation extract; a listed orphan that later resolves to an ACE row is no longer listed, because the owner's REC-05 step resolves it and the harness only reads the result. P1 owns every state change in this story: the cutover load writes the migrated records in its own schema through its own Flyway sequence, JOB-04 writes the reconciliation result and the break rows, and rwb-case serves the case it already holds. The harness reads those states and sets none of them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the break list and the run report (Platform administration R); signs the reconciliation of the business date |
| RW-COE, centre of excellence | Reads the break list and the report (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the break list, the report and the run evidence (Platform administration R) |
| RW-COMPLY, compliance | Reads the break list and the report (Platform administration R) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the break list and restarts the run for a business date (Platform administration R) |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Reads the run evidence (Platform administration R) |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real owner |
| P1 rwb-source-data identity | Serves the data product records, the freshness, the interactions and the JOB-04 rerun, and owns every migration and reconciliation write |
| P3 rwb-case identity | Serves the case, its stage and its primary person key |

No role outside the six above reads the break list: a caller with role RW-OFF and no Platform administration right is refused with MSG-P4-002. No level of the delegation of authority applies, because the harness takes no business decision.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Owning schema | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055 | recovery_case | rwb_case (P3) | all fields, case_no, primary_person_key and stage_code included | Read through the rwb-case contract |
| DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-029 | interaction | rwb_source_data (P1) | all fields, case_id, person_key, contact_key, promise date and promise amount included | Read through the rwb-source-data contract |
| DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026 | contact_point_ext | rwb_source_data (P1) | all fields, contact_key and contact_type included | Read through the rwb-source-data contract |
| Standard column | interaction, recovery_case, contact_point_ext | the owner's schema | source, migrated_at | Read through the owner's contract |

DP02 Customer and party holds v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact for the person_key and the contact_key, and DP05 Contact and promises holds v_ace_efs_action, v_ace_efs_action_code, v_ace_efs_assignment and interaction (FSD P1 v3). The harness owns no table and writes no row: it reads the records through rwb-source-data's contract and the case through rwb-case's contract (DP-01, DP-05). The EFS history is twelve months of ACE data read through the views under DL29, and the harness asserts it is read and never stored. The synthetic promise amount 12500 is the monthly instalment of the worked example in the Temporal and Drools design, used as a fixture value and not as a business parameter.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | Trigger JOB-04 for the business date under test, and the rerun of AC4, each with one Idempotency-Key |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP02/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Resolve the person_key and the contact_key against v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP05/records?caseId={caseId}` | P1 rwb-source-data | Read the promise and the EFS history of the case (AC1, AC2, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness?product=DP05` | P1 rwb-source-data | The data date of DP05 before the run, and the late-batch refusal of X5 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The migrated interaction INT-0605 and its promise date and amount (AC1, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case, its stage and its primary person key (AC1) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and Platform administration right for every call, including the refusal of AC5 |

Every operation is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget and a circuit breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-13). This legacy key has no screen, so no gateway-bff composite route is called: DP-19 is recorded for the wave's screen path only. No operation is invented in this story, and none of them is a table read or a view read.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it reads the owner's answer and writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. JOB-04 is triggered through the owner's rerun operation and not by publishing AceDataReady; the event-triggered start of JOB-04 is the behaviour RWB-P1-DM005-APP owns, and the harness asserts the result and not the trigger.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises the existing JOB-04 reconciliation workflow and its REC-05 step on the owner's task queue `rwb-source-data` and asserts their effects through the owner's contract; no workflow, activity or task queue is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. JOB-04 is event-triggered in rwb-source-data, and the harness reruns it for a business date through the owner's operation, so no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window is set by this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); `interaction` and `contact_point_ext` are rwb-source-data's, `recovery_case` is rwb-case's, and the harness reads every one of them through the owning contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Use in the run |
|---|---|---|
| WireMock stub for rwb-source-data | The JOB-04 rerun, the DP02 and DP05 record reads, the DP05 freshness read and the interaction read | Day-1 run of AC1 to AC5 before RWB-P1-DM005-APP is live |
| WireMock stub for rwb-case | `GET /cases/{caseId}` | Day-1 assertion on the case, its stage and its primary person key |
| WireMock stub for rwb-access | `POST /authorise` | Day-1 authorisation and the refusal path of AC5 |
| Cutover extract fixture | The synthetic extract of the open promises and contact notes held outside EFS | The migrated records the harness expects on case RW-2026-000605, with the orphan contact key CP-SYN-0777 |
| Reconciliation extract fixture | The break list of the business date | The one-row break list of AC3 and the one-row rerun of AC4 |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The harness environment and its base hosts, the cutover extract fixture and its field layout, the reconciliation extract format and its retention, the pass or fail gate and the data seeding set are: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop each on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13); no screen composes this answer |
| Kafka | None published and none consumed; JOB-04 is triggered through the owner's operation |
| Temporal | None added; the JOB-04 reconciliation workflow and its REC-05 step are exercised on queue `rwb-source-data` |
| File | The cutover extract fixture and the reconciliation extract fixture, both synthetic and both read as files |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies in the table above (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty. The one blocking dependency is the I story RWB-P1-DM005-APP; until it lands the run uses the stub set and the report says so.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the five criteria in order for a business date, holds the run lock and writes one report per business date |
| StubSet | Fake | The three WireMock stubs generated from the published contracts, with the contract version pinned |
| CutoverExtractFixture | Fixture | The synthetic extract of the open promises and contact notes, with the case, person_key, contact_key, promise date and promise amount of the criteria and the orphan contact key |
| ContactKeyResolver | Service | Resolves the person_key and the contact_key through DP02 and reads the promise and the EFS history through DP05 with its freshness |
| BreakListAssertion | Service | Reads the reconciliation extract and asserts the break rows, their key type, their key value, their reason and their owner role |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes the per-run report keyed by story and business date, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real owner as RWB-P1-DM005-APP lands, on case `RW-2026-000605`, interaction `INT-0605` with person_key `PERS-SYN-0605`, contact_key `CP-SYN-0605`, promise date 2026-12-15 and promise amount 12500, the orphan contact_key `CP-SYN-0777` and business date 2026-11-30. Seeding is the cutover load of the owner's Flyway sequence, never a schema write by the harness. The environment, the fixture field layout, the extract format and the evidence retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the three stubs from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a version mismatch (X1).
2. Build the CutoverExtractFixture with the synthetic values of section 13 and the required-key check of X2.
3. Build the JourneyRunner for AC1: trigger JOB-04 with one Idempotency-Key, read interaction INT-0605 and the case, and assert the case, person_key, contact_key, promise date and promise amount (X2).
4. Add the ContactKeyResolver over DP02 and DP05 with the DP05 freshness read, and assert that no EFS row is in the ledger and that the source and migration date are present (X6, X5).
5. Add the BreakListAssertion for AC2 and AC3: every key resolves, and the orphan CP-SYN-0777 is listed once with key type CONTACT, reason NO_ACE_ROW and owner role RW-DATASTEW (X3).
6. Add the AC4 rerun with a second Idempotency-Key, the count comparison and the one-entry-per-business-date check (X4).
7. Add the AC5 access path through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` with the 403 and MSG-P4-002 refusal, then the EvidenceReport and the gate, and rerun the five criteria against the real owner when RWB-P1-DM005-APP lands (X7).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness runs behind no feature switch, and it reads no flag of its own.

**Done when.** The four test cases of section 16 pass against the three stubs on Day 1 and again against RWB-P1-DM005-APP when it lands; the break list holds one row for the orphan; the rerun is deterministic; and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and business date with the contract versions and whether each hop was a stub or the owner.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The DP05 freshness is late, so JOB-04 refuses the run | {product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A fixture row lacks a required field | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without the Platform administration right asks for the run | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness produces none of these messages itself; it asserts the message the owning service returns and names the message ID in the report, so a failure points at a service and a message and not only at a date.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story has no screen, and the harness renders none. What the wave entry check reads instead is the reconciliation extract for the business date, whose states are these:

| State | What the extract shows |
|---|---|
| No break | No row for the business date, and the run report records the counts of interactions and promise links that were checked |
| Break | One row per orphan: the interaction, the key type, the key value, the reason NO_ACE_ROW and the owner role RW-DATASTEW |

The SCR-45 data quality console is not part of this legacy key and is not read by this harness; the breaks reach the data steward and the ACE team through the reconciliation extract the legacy story names. The extract format, its retention and the report shape are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0445; ASM-0637).

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the promise dates and amounts, the reasons, the owner roles and the fixture values are data and SIT configuration, never constants of the harness.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures or reports: the contact values never appear, the fixtures are synthetic keys, and the report names identifiers and counts only.
- No cross-schema read and no direct view read: every field comes through the owning service's contract (DP-01, DP-05), and only rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_* (ADR-010, D-RCV-35).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real-service pass: the report names the contract version and whether each hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never seeds a migrated record, sets a break row or resolves an orphan by hand.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the service that owns it or reported as a gap; it is never waived in the script (DL25).

Change log: v1, 22 November 2026, D-RCV-60, T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a data steward, I want the listings, the case asset links and the open sale instructions migrated from the legacy Workbench, so that an asset already offered for sale is not lost at cutover while the collateral, appraisal and NPA asset records are read from ACE.

After the realignment this story carries the part of that sentence that belongs to `rwb-source-data`:

- the appraisal-acceptance decision, held in the extension table `valuation_ext` and keyed by `valuation_key`, because it is a Workbench decision about an ACE appraisal and not a copy of it;
- the DP06 read path — `v_ace_collateral`, `v_ace_collateral_detail`, `v_ace_valuation`, `v_ace_asset`, `v_ace_npa_asset`, `v_ace_npa_sale` — read through the service's own views and its published contract, never a `public.*` table;
- the cutover gate for DP06 in the service's own schema: the migration run, its break list and the evidence the data steward signs off.

The `listing` and `asset_sale` rows are not in the `rwb_source_data` table list. The owning service for those two tables is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2167; ASM-3479); the default ruling of this story places them with `rwb-asset` (S5), read through that service's contract mock in AC1 (ASM-3479).

##### 2. Business rationale

An asset already offered for sale must survive the switch from the legacy Workbench to the 19 services. Under the realignment nothing of the collateral or NPA estate is carried across: ACE holds it, ingested from CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and RPS, and the Workbench reads it (DP-05). What the Workbench does own is the decision about an appraisal — accepted, by whom, when, which panel valuer, stale after its cycle — and that decision belongs in exactly one schema.

Two consequences drive this story:

1. **One number, one source.** DP06 "Collateral and assets" names one system of record for each part: ACE for the collateral, appraisal, NPA asset and NPA sale records, the Workbench for the appraisal acceptance and the sale instruction. Copying an ACE row into `rwb_source_data` would create a second copy that disagrees with ACE and is owned by nobody who maintains the source (D-RCV-35 U1).
2. **Cutover is a data decision, not a deployment step.** The legacy estate is a live estate: a property listed for auction, a sale instruction open with a vendor and an appraisal accepted last month are all in flight at the switch. The cutover therefore keeps a gate — extract, map to business keys, load, check, sign off — and the gate is only passed on evidence.

DP-15 puts the migration on the service's own Flyway sequence, so the change ships with the service and rolls back with it, and DP-19 keeps the data quality screen behind one gateway-bff composite route, so the service exposes no screen of its own.

##### 3. Preconditions

| # | Precondition |
|---|---|
| 1 | The `rwb_source_data` schema, its login and the 92-table baseline including the four extension tables are deployed, `valuation_ext` among them (RWB-P1-E1001-APP). |
| 2 | The 16 Section A views and the 14 Section B views are deployed and the conformance test is green; the Section B views over `valuation`, `collateral_detail`, `npa_asset` and `npa_sale` need RWB-ACE-001 (RWB-P1-E1069-APP; DL43). |
| 3 | The per-service Flyway sequence is available at the next free version in `rwb_source_data` (DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). |
| 4 | The data quality screen is reachable through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON). |
| 5 | The user holds Platform administration, right R: RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM or RW-SECADM (legacy RWB-DM-006 permission table; TSD P1 T6.1). |
| 6 | The legacy Workbench tables are available read only for the one-off extract, and the ACE batch record shows a COMPLETED row for every DP06 source for the cutover business date (T3.7). |

##### 4. Flow

| Step | Actor | Action | System response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | System (recovery service identity) | Reads the legacy listing, case asset link, sale instruction and appraisal acceptance records at cutover | Rejects a row with no `asset_key` or no `valuation_key`, counts it and lists it |
| 2 | System | Maps each row to the new schema: acceptance to `valuation_ext` by `valuation_key`, every asset link to `asset_key` as `varchar(255)` with no foreign key | Applies BR-P1-001-3 and BR-P1-001-5 |
| 3 | System | Runs the cutover migration at the next free Flyway version in `rwb_source_data` | Commits one batch, writes the row count per object, leaves no partial load |
| 4 | System | Checks the DP06 read path: the six DP06 views answer and `valuation_ext` joins `v_ace_valuation` 1:1 | Writes the break list and the orphan list |
| 5 | System | Publishes the cutover evidence to the reconciliation extract behind SCR-45 Data quality | Shows counts, breaks and the DP06 freshness stamp (LOADED or STALE) |
| 6 | Data steward | Reviews the breaks and signs off (section 10) | Records the sign-off |
| 7 | System | Serves the migrated records from `rwb_source_data` and keeps the legacy tables read only | Cutover complete |

##### 5. Exception paths

| # | Condition | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A legacy row carries no `asset_key` or no `valuation_key` | The row is refused, counted and listed for the data steward; nothing is written for it (BR-P1-001-3). |
| 2 | A `valuation_key` has no row in `v_ace_valuation` | The REC-05 orphan is listed for the data steward and the ACE team; no Workbench record is deleted or changed (BR-P1-011-3). |
| 3 | Section B is not deployed when the cutover runs | The acceptance rows stay behind their feature flag, DP06 shows STALE with no business date, and the cutover is not signed off (T3.7, DL43). |
| 4 | A view returns an error during the check | No reconciliation row is written for the business date; the run shows FAILED with MSG-GEN-006 for system "ACE database"; the rerun from the job monitor writes the rows. |
| 5 | The migration is run twice | Flyway reports the version as already applied; the row counts per object are unchanged; no batch is written twice. |
| 6 | A user without the right tries the action | Refused with MSG-P4-002; nothing changes. |
| 7 | The legacy tables are held read only past the retention period | The period is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2168; ASM-3480); the default in ASM-2 applies. |

##### 6. INVEST check

| I | Independent | Yes: one service, one schema, one Flyway version; it builds against CON stories and their fakes. |
| N | Negotiable | Yes: the break thresholds and the evidence format are open until the PRD (C1). |
| V | Valuable | Yes: an asset in flight at cutover is not lost, and DP06 has one owner per number. |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Migrate collateral and assets

  Scenario: AC1 Extract the Workbench records (legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1)
    Given the rwb-asset contract mock returns the listing and asset_sale records for each asset_key
    Given the legacy Workbench listing, case asset link, sale instruction and appraisal acceptance records at cutover
    When the migration reads them
    Then each listing and each sale carries its asset_key, and each appraisal decision its valuation_key
    And no collateral, appraisal, NPA asset or NPA sale record is copied, because each is read from v_ace_collateral, v_ace_valuation, v_ace_asset, v_ace_npa_asset or v_ace_npa_sale

  Scenario: AC3 Cut over (legacy RWB-DM-006 AC3)
    Given ten clean days on the migrated records
    When the data steward signs off
    Then the legacy tables stay read-only for their retention period
    And the migrated records are served from the new schema
```

The legacy AC2 (reconcile the business keys, the REC-05 step) is not owned by this story; it sits with the reconciliation deliverable of the same legacy key, together with TC-DM-006-02 (ASM-3482).

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Rule text (legacy wording kept, schema named for this service) |
|---|---|
| BR-P1-001-2 | The recovery module reads ACE only through `recovery.v_ace_*` — here `rwb_source_data`'s own `v_ace_*` views. A direct `public.*` read in a story, spec or query is a defect. |
| BR-P1-001-3 | No constraint in this service's schema references a table outside it. A link to a source record is a business-key column of type `varchar(255)` with no foreign key. |
| BR-P1-001-5 | An extension table holds a Workbench decision about an ACE record and never a copy of an ACE column. It is 1:1 with the ACE record and carries the seven standard record columns. |
| BR-P1-011-3 | A REC-05 orphan never deletes or changes a Workbench record; it is listed for the data steward and, where the row is missing in ACE, for the ACE team. |
| BR-P1-014-3 | A product fed by more than one source carries the oldest business date among its sources, and is STALE while any of them is late. DP06 is fed by CCMS, SVAF, AMIS and RPS. |
| DP-15 | The migration runs at the next free Flyway version in `rwb_source_data`. No object is created in another service's schema and no shared baseline is reused. |
| DP-19 | The data quality screen is one gateway-bff composite route. The service publishes no screen route of its own. |

##### 9. State transitions

State names for a migration batch are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2169; ASM-3481). The transitions below use the existing lists LOV-FRESHNESS (LOADED, STALE) and the cutover gate of AC3.

| From | To | Trigger | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | Extracted | the cutover run reads the legacy records | row count per legacy object |
| Extracted | Loaded | the Flyway version commits in `rwb_source_data` | row count per object; DP06 LOADED |
| Loaded | Reconciled | REC-05 lists no orphan for `asset_key` and `valuation_key` | empty orphan list |
| Reconciled | Signed off | the data steward signs off | sign-off recorded; ten clean days of AC3 |
| Signed off | Cut over | the cutover date arrives | legacy tables read only; records served from `rwb_source_data` |
| Loaded, Reconciled | Held | an orphan, a refused row or a missing Section B view | break list on SCR-45: Data quality |
| LOADED | STALE | a DP06 source batch is late or failed | DP06 freshness stamp (T3.7) |

##### 10. Authority

| Decision | Role that holds it | Right |
|---|---|---|
| Run or rerun the cutover migration | Platform administrator (RW-PLATADM) | Platform administration, C and U |
| Read the break list and the cutover evidence | RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | Platform administration, R |
| Sign off the cutover | Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW) | Platform administration, R, as the legacy RWB-DM-006 permission table gives it |
| Change the reconciliation tolerance used by AC3 | Decision DL25 | n/a; the tolerance is a parameter, not a code value |

The story starts no approval workflow and holds no authority of its own; every action is checked by the capability area of the screen or the job, and the sign-off is the data steward's right, not a new role.

##### 12. Contract

**12.1 REST operations provided**

None. The legacy story states that it has no endpoint: "the migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity, and its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract." The realignment keeps that, so this story adds no operation to `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`.

**12.2 REST operations consumed**

| Operation | Service | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness | rwb-source-data (own service) | Reads the DP06 stamp (LOADED or STALE) for the cutover evidence |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP06/records | rwb-source-data (own service) | Proves the migrated records and the ACE views answer together after the cutover |
| GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/reconciliation/results | rwb-source-data (own service) | Reads the REC-05 orphan list that gates the sign-off |

No operation of another service is called; the `rwb-asset` payload in AC1 is a contract fake (12.8).

**12.3 Events published**

None. The migration publishes no fact; EV-26 AceDataReady and EV-27 AceDataLate (`rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1`) belong to the freshness story.

**12.4 Events consumed**

None.

**12.5 Workflows and activities**

None. The service runs no Temporal workflow for this story and the queue `rwb-source-data` carries none; the cutover is a one-off migration run, not a workflow.

**12.6 Schedules**

None. The cutover is a one-off run at the cutover date, not a Temporal Schedule; JOB-01 and JOB-09 are retired and JOB-04 is the daily reconciliation of the case list, delivered elsewhere.

**12.7 Tables owned**

| Schema | Table | Key | Written by this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb_source_data | valuation_ext | valuation_key, `varchar(255)`, no foreign key | Yes: one row per acceptance, with the seven standard columns |

`listing` and `asset_sale` are not in this schema (GAP-2167; ASM-3479).

**12.8 Contract fakes**

| Fake | Used for | Values kept |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb-asset` contract fake | The listing and asset_sale payload of AC1 | `asset_key` on every listing and every sale |

**12.9 Call-type summary**

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Three own-service reads of 12.2; no other service is called |
| Kafka | No | No event is published or consumed |
| Temporal | No | No workflow, activity or task queue |
| File | Yes | One cutover evidence extract (counts, breaks, orphan list) handed to SCR-45 |

| Component | Work in this story |

| Cutover migration | One new Flyway version on the `rwb_source_data` sequence (DP-15): inserts `valuation_ext` from the legacy extract by `valuation_key`, rerun safe, one transaction per batch |
| RecoveryDataEngineService | Maps the extract, applies BR-P1-001-3 and BR-P1-001-5, counts rows per object, builds the break and orphan lists |
| RecoveryDataEngineRepository | Reads and writes `valuation_ext` only; no other table of the schema is touched |

No view, dictionary row or schema object is created: those are the H dependencies (`RWB-P1-E1001-APP`, `RWB-P1-E1069-APP`). The `rwb-asset` side of the payload is not built here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version (BR-P1-001).
- No personal data in logs, tests, prompts or the cutover extract: the extract carries keys and counts, never a name, an identity number or a contact value.
- ACE data only through this service's own `v_ace_*` views or its published contract; a `public.*` read is a defect.
- No foreign key from `rwb_source_data` into ACE, and no copy of an ACE collateral, appraisal, NPA asset or NPA sale row.
- The legacy tables are read only; the migration never writes to the legacy Workbench.
- The migration is rerun safe and leaves no partial load.
